identity.name: Santos de Cartier

case.bezel: polished steel bezel with exposed screws

identity.one_liner: The large steel Santos from Cartier's 2018 relaunch, using a tool-free quick-change bracelet system and the brand's own automatic caliber.

narrative.story: Cartier's Santos line traces to 1904, when Louis Cartier built a wristwatch for his friend, the aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont, so he could check the time without taking a hand off the controls during flight — commonly cited as one of the first purpose-made men's wristwatches rather than a converted pocket watch. Cartier relaunched the Santos de Cartier in 2018 with a redesigned case, exposed bezel screws referencing the original, and a tool-free quick-change bracelet system that swaps between metal bracelet and leather strap.
narrative.collector_notes: Bracelet link removal on this generation uses a push-button system rather than pins; confirm all original links are present, since replacement links are Cartier-specific parts rather than generic steel links.
